embedModal.title: Embed this viewer
embedModal.intro: Generate a link or <iframe> to drop this interactive 3D IFC viewer into a blog post, article, or CDE panel.
embedModal.modelUrlHelp: The file must be reachable over HTTPS and allow cross-origin (CORS) requests.
embedModal.noUrl: Enter a public IFC URL above to generate the embed code.
embedModal.corsNote: The model is fetched in the visitor's browser — it never touches our servers. The host must send CORS headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin) for the file to load.
embedModal.whereHint: Paste into a blog, a CDE panel, Notion, a Power BI “Web content” visual or any dashboard.
embedModal.sunOn: Open the sun study on load
embedModal.sunEvergreen: Leave the year out and the link stays evergreen — the same day, every year.
embedModal.siteNote: Needs a georeferenced model. Streams map and terrain tiles from third parties, and OpenStreetMap data must stay attributed — enabling this makes that call for your page’s visitors.

exportModal.title: Export
exportModal.ifcNotAvailable: IFC buffer not available (model loaded from fragments cache only)
exportModal.advancedHint: What the exported file says about itself. IFC records this in its STEP header, and it is what a recipient reads to tell your file apart from what the authoring tool shipped.
exportModal.stampHeader: Record this export in the file
exportModal.stampOn: Sets the write date to now and the writing tool to {{app}}. The authoring application is left as it was — the model still came from there.
exportModal.stampOff: The header will keep the original tool and date, so the file will look untouched even if you edited it.
exportModal.author: Author
exportModal.blankKeeps: Leave a field blank to keep whatever the file already carried.
exportModal.schemaNote: The IFC schema is never changed. A file opened as IFC2x3 is exported as IFC2x3.
